desc.Tamale: A tamale is a Mesoamerican dish of masa dough made from corn, filled with meats, cheeses, vegetables, or chilies. The filling is wrapped in a corn husk or banana leaf and steamed, resulting in a soft, moist texture with savory or sweet flavors depending on the filling.
desc.Alfajor: Alfajores are South American sandwich cookies made from two shortbread-like biscuits joined by a layer of dulce de leche caramel. They are often dusted with powdered sugar and served as a sweet treat, tasting buttery, rich, and caramel-sweet.
desc.English breakfast tea: English breakfast tea is a robust, full-bodied black tea blend typically made from Assam, Ceylon, and Kenyan teas. It is brewed strong, often served hot with milk and sugar to complement its rich, malty flavor that pairs well with hearty meals.
desc.Ale: Ale is a style of beer brewed using warm fermentation with malted barley and a bittering agent like hops. It is served in pubs and bars, typically with a balanced malt sweetness and hop bitterness resulting in flavors ranging from fruity to robust.
desc.Currywurst: Currywurst is a popular German fast food consisting of sliced pork sausage topped with a spicy curry ketchup sauce. It is served hot at street stands and restaurants, often with french fries, offering a savory, mildly spicy and tangy taste.
desc.Weißwurst: Weisswurst is a fresh Bavarian sausage made from minced veal and pork fatback, flavored with parsley, lemon, and spices like mace and ginger. It is poached and traditionally served hot at restaurants with sweet mustard and a pretzel, having a mild, delicate flavor.
desc.Schweinshaxe: Schweinshaxe is a roasted pork knuckle with crispy skin and tender meat. It is slow-roasted until the fat renders, served hot in Bavarian restaurants with a rich, savory taste and often accompanied by potato dumplings and sauerkraut.
desc.Eisbein: Eisbein is a German dish of corned and slightly boiled ham hock. It is served tender and flavorful in restaurants, typically with sauerkraut and mashed potatoes or peas, offering a salty, smoky pork taste.
desc.Goulash: Goulash is a hearty stew made with chunks of meat and vegetables seasoned primarily with paprika. It is slow-cooked until the meat is tender, served hot in Central European restaurants with a rich, savory and mildly spicy flavor.
desc.Knödel: Knödel are boiled dumplings made from flour, bread, or potatoes, often served as a side dish. They have a soft, dense texture and mild taste, commonly accompanying meats or served in soup in Central European cafés and restaurants.
desc.Spätzle: Spätzle are soft, egg-based pasta dumplings with an irregular shape and rough texture. They are boiled or steamed and often served as a side to sauced meats or as a main with cheese and onions, having a mild, chewy taste in German and Austrian restaurants.
desc.Flammekueche: Flammkuchen is a thin, rectangular flatbread topped with crème fraîche, sliced onions, and lardons. It is baked quickly in a hot oven until crispy and served sliced in Alsatian and German restaurants, tasting creamy, savory, and slightly smoky.
desc.Blood sausage: Blutwurst is a sausage made from cooked animal blood mixed with fillers like meat, fat, and grains. It is sliced and served hot or cold in European restaurants, with a rich, earthy, and mildly spiced flavor depending on the recipe.
desc.Leberkäse: Leberkäse is a finely ground loaf of beef, pork, and bacon baked in a pan to form a crispy crust. It is sliced and served hot in southern German and Austrian restaurants, often in a roll with mustard, offering a savory, meaty taste without actual liver.
desc.Wheat beer: Weissbier is a top-fermented wheat beer brewed with a high proportion of wheat malt. It is cloudy, effervescent, and served in tall glasses in German beer halls and cafés, with a refreshing, fruity, and spicy taste from yeast and wheat.
desc.Full breakfast: A full English breakfast is a hearty cooked meal featuring fried eggs, bacon, sausages, black pudding, grilled tomatoes, mushrooms, and toasted or fried bread. It is served on a large plate, often accompanied by baked beans, and is rich, savory, and filling.
desc.Black pudding: Black pudding is a blood sausage made primarily from pork blood, fat, and oatmeal or barley, seasoned with herbs and spices. It is sliced and pan-fried until crispy on the outside and soft inside, offering a savory, earthy, and mildly spicy taste.
desc.Pasty: A Cornish pasty is a baked hand pie with a shortcrust pastry shell folded around a filling of diced beef, potato, onion, and swede, crimped at the edge. It is served hot or at room temperature, with a savory, hearty flavor from the seasoned meat and vegetables.
desc.Yorkshire pudding: Yorkshire pudding is a light, puffed baked item made from a simple batter of eggs, flour, and milk that rises to form a crisp exterior and soft, airy interior. It is commonly served as a side with roast dinners, often filled with gravy for a savory, comforting taste.
desc.Roast beef: Roast beef is a large cut of beef slow-roasted until tender and juicy, typically served sliced in thick portions as the centerpiece of a meal. It has a rich, savory flavor enhanced by its natural juices and is often accompanied by gravy and sides like Yorkshire pudding.
desc.Toad in the hole: Toad in the hole is a dish of sausages baked within a large Yorkshire pudding batter until the batter is golden and risen. It is usually served with onion gravy, mashed potatoes, and vegetables, delivering a savory, comforting taste with crispy batter and juicy sausages.
desc.Shepherd's pie: Cottage pie is a baked savory dish of minced beef mixed with vegetables and gravy, topped with a layer of creamy mashed potatoes that becomes golden and crisp in the oven. It offers a hearty, comforting taste with savory meat and smooth, buttery potato.
desc.Sausage roll: A sausage roll is a savory pastry consisting of seasoned sausage meat encased in flaky puff pastry and baked until golden and crisp. It is often served hot or at room temperature as a snack or party food, with a juicy, herby sausage flavor inside a buttery crust.
desc.Trifle: Trifle is a layered dessert with sponge cake or ladyfingers soaked in sherry, fruit or jelly, creamy custard, and whipped cream, assembled in a glass dish to show the distinct layers. It is served chilled, offering a sweet, creamy taste with soft, fruity, and spongy textures.
desc.Crumpet: A crumpet is a small, round, spongy bread made from a batter of flour, milk or water, and yeast, cooked on a griddle to develop a porous top and crisp base. It is typically toasted and served with butter that melts into the holes, providing a chewy, yeasty taste.
desc.English muffin: An English muffin is a small, round, flat yeast bread with a slightly crisp exterior and soft, nooks-and-crannies interior, cooked on a griddle. It is split, toasted, and served with butter, jam, or savory toppings like eggs and bacon for a chewy, mildly tangy flavor.
desc.Chocolate chip cookie: A chocolate chip cookie is a drop cookie containing pieces of chocolate mixed into the dough before baking. It can range from moist and chewy to crispy in texture and is typically sweet with a buttery flavor from the dough and melty chocolate bits.
desc.Croque monsieur: A croque monsieur is a hot sandwich made with ham and cheese, typically gruyère. It is often assembled with buttered bread, then toasted or fried until golden and melty, sometimes topped with béchamel sauce for added creaminess.
desc.Castella: Castella is a Japanese sponge cake known for its sweet, moist brioche-style flavor and texture. It is made with eggs, sugar, flour, and syrup, baked in rectangular molds to create a soft, springy cake that is often sliced and served plain.
